children: Stablecoin holdings among large investors in the cryptocurrency market have fallen sharply, raising concerns that potential buying power is weakening.
Santiment said on Nov. 21 that balances in the top 100 whale wallets holding the most Tether
on the Ethereum network have dropped by $15.14 billion since the start of the year. That represents a 21.1% decline from the beginning of the year.
Over the same period, balances in the top 100 whale wallets holding USD Coin
on the Ethereum network fell by $6.72 billion. The decline was 23.7%, steeper than the drop in USDT.

Stablecoins are considered sidelined capital that can be deployed immediately to buy Bitcoin and altcoins. As a result, stablecoin holdings among large investors are used as a gauge of the crypto market's potential buying power.

Still, a decline in stablecoin balances does not necessarily mean funds have left the market. Santiment said the money may have been used to buy cryptocurrencies, redeemed, or moved to other networks or wallets.
The drop in USDT and USDC concentrated among large holders suggests the market is showing less capital waiting on the sidelines to be deployed than before, according to Santiment.

That means future fund flows and buying activity will need to be monitored to determine whether the decline in stablecoin balances held by whale wallets leads to an actual reduction in market liquidity.

title: Stablecoin Whale Holdings Plunge, Fueling Concern Over Crypto Buying Power
